statement: A commit-time candidate whose changed-path count exceeds the scope-pressure limit is admitted without an operator override exactly when the excess paths are the recorded same-base rejected-candidate replacement superset re-derived from recorded attempts' own change artifacts, while forged, drifted, non-applicable, or foreign-base rejection records leave the scope guard fail-closed.

constraints.statement: If this Quest changes source code, spawn a subagent verifier before audit and git handoff, then record a Solver finding with evidence subagent:<id>.

The exemption set is the union of requiredPaths from replacementRequirementGroups (checkpoint-preflight.js), which re-derives paths live from recorded attempts' change artifacts; no path may enter the exemption from rejection receipt text, operator input, or any source that is not a recorded attempt's own inspected artifact.

replacementRequirementGroups is exported from checkpoint-preflight.js and consumed at the step.js/attempt.js call sites; the superset computation is not reimplemented, and scope-pressure.js gains no import of verification.js (measured cycle risk).

Before wiring, a finding records the measured wall-clock cost of computing verificationState at the commit-time call sites on a representative multi-attempt quest log; if it exceeds one second the exemption computes lazily, only when the scope guard would otherwise block.

Closure evidence includes adversarial cases proving a forged fingerprint, a drifted sealed artifact, a foreign-base rejection, and an already-discharged rejection each leave the guard blocking, and that override budget accounting (guard-override events) is unchanged for genuinely out-of-superset excess.

The operator override path for blocked-scope remains available and its recorded semantics are unchanged; the exemption removes only the deterministic overrides whose reason is the mandatory replacement superset itself (measured 2026-07-28: three such overrides in eight minutes on comparative-efficiency-measured-cell-admission).
